utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Velic, according to the information I have, you had the main say in your municipality regarding all decisions that were taken at the time. Is it true that Semsudin Velic, your own brother, was appointed head of the Secretariat of the Interior precisely at your proposal?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct because at the time when he was appointed to that position I was not president of the SDA of Bosanska Krupa at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not president, okay, but was he appointed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was appointed immediately after the multi-party elections, and I was elected president of the SDA only a year later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it true that the secretary of the Executive Board was Edhem Dizdarevic, your relative?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Edhem Dizdarevic was secretary of the Executive Board but I'm not aware that he's my relative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it true that Suad Alibegic, president of the Executive Board, was appointed at your proposal?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late Suad Alibegovic -- Alibegic, who died in a car accident, was appointed at the proposal of the independent municipality of Buzim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not involved?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was not involved because I did not know Mr. Alibegic at all at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it true that your uncle Omer Velic held one of the managerial positions in Krupatrans company?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only one uncle, Kasim Velic. He was never employed with that company in Bosanska Krupa. He worked abroad in Austria.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is this Omer Velic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the gentleman but we are not related.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Omer Velic, but we are not related, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were not involved in any of these appointments, were you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the appointment of my brother Semsudin Velic, chief of the police station is concerned, I was not involved directly because I was only a member of the Executive Board of the SDA of Bosanska Krupa at that moment. And as far as the appointment of Omer Alibegic is concerned, I was not involved because he was nominated by an independent organisation of the municipality of Buzim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was your influence on it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My influence was limited to presenting my positions and arguments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in paragraph 4 you said that problems in the interrelations between the SDS and the SDA in the area of Krupa resulted from the -- their attitude towards the role of the JNA in the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that statement with me. It hadn't been given to me. But problems did arise around that, because the SDA and the SDA [as interpreted] had different positions -- had different views on the role of the JNA in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 4 that you didn't agree with the JNA being used to resolve problems in Croatia. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask me directly about --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about your opinion, I'm asking you about your statement.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find this passage at the moment, so I cannot comment upon it, but in any case, I did not agree nor would I agree today with the use of the JNA in any internal conflict in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about the resolution of political problems in the former Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is a wrong interpretation of my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A wrong interpretation of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could not give me the example of a single political problem in Croatia where the JNA would be involved?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to be more specific. I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that this is a wrong interpretation of your statement because the resolution of political problems in Croatia was not something the JNA was involved in or interfered with?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say it was a wrong interpretation of my statement because political divergences in the multi-party political life of Croatia were what they were. It was only later that the JNA -- in fact, even later the JNA did not interfere with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you consider as taking sides on the part of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanding staff of the JNA were never given the opportunity to present their views publicly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In 1991, the year you are referring to, Bosnia and Herzegovina was an integral part of Yugoslavia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose you agree, both as a lawyer, former judge, public prosecutor, a person who is familiar with the law, that with the decision on mobilisation that was adopted then by the federal authorities, the decision was binding on everybody regardless of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware that the decision on mobilisation that was then adopted was adopted by federal authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say on page 4 in paragraph 2 that the SDS wanted to have direct control over personal documents of military conscripts in Bosanska Krupa. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant, actually, was that the SDS wanted to dispose of the military documentation of military conscripts of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they wanted to have the documentation of military conscripts of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In inter-party negotiations, representatives of the SDS were explicit. They wanted the documentation of military conscripts of Serb ethnicity to be separated from the rest so that they could dispose of it and mobilise these conscripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I suppose that you imply the files, the military files of these conscripts, not their personal documents.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that the following imprecision is also accidental: The documents did not belong to the conscripts. They belonged to the military authorities that were part of the -- that had the Territorial Defence as its integral part.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this documentation was held by the Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On their premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, as you say, that the head of the Secretariat for National Defence was a Serb, a man named Boro?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you don't know his exact name but he was a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was nominated to that position by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it possible, then, that this man Boro, who was head of that secretariat, was unable to get hold of that documentation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was of course authorised, as all the other senior staff of the secretariat, to handle their documentation and use it for purposes envisaged by the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he had access to that documentation and was able to use it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He had every legal authority to review and use that documentation in keeping with the decisions of the competent authorities. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in paragraph 12 you say that the SDS was denied this so-called control by the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS could not have control of that documentation. Only authorised officers were able to handle the documentation, and that's how you should understand my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does it mean, then, that the SDS -- sorry, the SDA had actual control of the documentation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean that. It means that the staff of the secretariat disposed of the documentation in the legally envisaged way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the question. This is going too fast. Would you please repeat the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Now -- just a moment. Both of you must bear in mind that this has to be interpreted. So, Mr. Milosevic, you know quite well, you've been here long enough to know that, so would you bear the interpreters in mind. We will go on from now. I don't think we'll be able to recover what the last question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Velic. In paragraph 3 on page 4, you say that after this decision was taken by the SDA, the JNA intervened, but: "The police and the civilians managed to prevent this, and the JNA did not attempt to do so." Is this a precise quotation of what you said?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read my statement correctly, but what does it mean? Perhaps I did not use the most precise terms. One day a small military unit came to Bosanska Krupa, to the office of the president of the municipality, Mehmed Mahic, and asked to take away the documentation from the Secretariat for National Defence. As far as I know, this was met with the dissatisfaction of a certain number of citizens who gathered on the premises of the Secretariat of National Defence. In talks with the president of the secretariat, Mehmed Mahic, the military abandoned the idea of taking this documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the JNA did not even try to intervene?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the term "intervention" is too strong. Armed soldiers, about 15 or 20 of them, did come, but they did not try to use force to take this documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct, though, that then in early autumn 1991, the documentation was the focus of negotiations between representatives of military authorities and local officials, representatives of the SDA rather than between the SDS and the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details of these negotiations. I did not even attend the talks between representatives of the municipality and the military. And I don't know if there were any other talks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But the talks were between military representatives and representatives of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not representatives of the SDA but official representatives of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were SDA members, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific example, Mr. Mehmed Mahic was a member of the SDA. He was president of the secretariat. If you give me another name, I'll be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that your wife was taking out this documentation on the quiet, on the sly, through the window while negotiations were going on, together with Semso Sepic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, sir. She was a member of the staff of the secretariat, that much is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Velic. You advocated the abolishing of the secretariat and its attachment to the secretariat of the economy.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot say that I personally advocated it. What is true is at the time a reorganisation of municipal administration bodies was under way. At that time, as far as I remember, there was a proposal to organise the Secretariat for National Defence as part of the Secretariat of the Economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what justification was given for that, pray?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I couldn't tell you now but there are documents about that and they can be made available to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell me, based on pure logic, what could be the justification for attaching the Secretariat of Defence to the Secretariat for Economy?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an explanation. I told you that I worked as president of the SDA from September 1991 as a volunteer, on voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on to another topic. In paragraph 5, page -- in paragraph 3, page 5, you say that in local commune of Otoka of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa there occurred an arrest of some people you refer to as Martic's policemen.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I assume that your brother knows a lot more about this incident, that is Semsudin Velic, the then chief of police.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess that's so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That same evening, as you mention, Martic himself was arrested who was together with Smiljanic, an officer of the JNA from the Banja Luka Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Perhaps arrest, it would be the wrong word, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, so what's the word you would use?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the previous events that took place with Martic's policemen, as I said, caused unrest among citizens in Bosanska Krupa because they were released from the Bosanska Krupa police station when yet another 20-odd policemen of Martic's came in. It was Sunday, the police station was not properly secured, and that's how this happened. I thought then and I think today that this was an armed provocation and an attempt to destabilise the situation in Bosanska Krajina, specifically in Bosanska Krupa. In view of the anxiety among the citizens themselves, in Otoka that evening about 500 to 1.000 citizens assembled around the bridge. It was in the early evening. There was a police checkpoint there for controlling traffic, and as the citizens assembled there, quite accidentally a vehicle came up and Mr. Martic and Mr. Smiljanic were in that vehicle. Since the citizens noticed SAO Krajina insignia on the uniforms of the persons in the vehicle, then this caused even greater unrest. The policemen who were present were compelled to transport this vehicle to the police station Otoka. It was only when he was identified at the police station that Martic was recognised and Smiljanic introduced himself as he offered his ID, his military ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say on page 5 of your statement -- because you say it just now, that arrest is not an adequate word -- you say: "That same evening Milan Martic, Serb commander from Croatia, was arrested near a small town called Otoka." I asked you about that and then you also referred to Colonel Smiljanic or, rather, Lieutenant Colonel Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question so there is no need to go over it again. He has explained the circumstances and what he means.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, who issued the order to arrest Martic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one. As a matter of fact, I've just said that "arrest" was not an adequate term at all, and it does not correspond to the situation in which this happened. That night I came to Otoka and I saw for myself that Martic was already there at the police station in Otoka and that he was actually protected by the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In view of the fact that your brother, as you said yourself, was the chief of police at the time, is it correct that under his command Muslim civilians were then given weapons by the police station Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in Bosanska Krupa?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that's not correct, Mr. Milosevic, but arms were distributed to the reserve police force, or rather, part of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So arms were distributed to part of the reserve police force as you put it. And then further on you say that the -- the order for Martic's arrest was annulled from Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when Martic was released, he was given an escort of the republican MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, he and Mr. Smiljanic were, and they were transported to Bosanski Novi. In Bosanski Novi, Mr. Mahic Mehmed was present, president of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa, who attended the meeting between Martic and Mladic, General Mladic, who at that time did not probably hold the rank of general. He deserved it later. It was a cordial meeting. It ended with a hug. And this is what Mahic told me about it: They were saying that the APB for Mr. Martic had been annulled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm quoting your statement. "An arrest warrant was issued for Martic, the Bosnian MUP intervened, and then he was sent back to Bosanski Novi. Mladic was waiting for him and the order was annulled from Belgrade." Do you allow for the following possibility, that it was not from Belgrade that the arrest warrant was annulled. It wasn't even issued by Belgrade but it was done by then minister of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Delimustafic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the APB or do you mean the arrest warrant? Well, as far as I know, what was made public then was there was a federal APB issued by the federal authorities but at the initiative of Croatia. However, it was annulled after what happened in Otoka and if we are to abide by the principles of legality, Mr. Delimustafic could not have annulled something that was issued by the federal authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know who annulled it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that while Martic was at the SUP premises in Krupa a large number of armed Muslims had assembled in front of the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Martic was never at the police station in Krupa, he was at the place station in Otoka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Otoka is in Krupa I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please speak one at a time, the interpreters ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're being asked again, you're being cautioned by the interpreters. Just leave a moment after the other has spoken, before you respond. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Otoka was a local commune within the municipality of Bosanska Krupa, and that is where the police department was, one of the police departments, and that is where Martic was during the night between the 8th and 9th of September, 1991. As I had already said, a number of citizens of Otoka had assembled in the centre of that area, but no, there was no harm done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, they had assembled and they wanted Martic to be handed over to them so that they could judge him.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, they had gathered there. Some of them were under the influence of alcohol, but the police held everything under control and there were no concrete requests put forth by the citizens, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On page 5, in paragraphs 9 and 11 you say that you from the Party of Democratic Action made every effort to increase the number of reservists of the police force and that that was the only way in which you could legally obtain weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This initiative was started in the autumn of 1991. Is that right, Mr. Velic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that initiative was launched much earlier, perhaps even about a year earlier, perhaps the spring of 1991, and it was launched from official quarters, the municipal authorities of Bosanska Krupa. It was also addressed to the appropriate authorities, that is to say the then-Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, why did you need weapons at the time, that is to say in the spring of 1991? There were no conflicts then. How did you know there would be some kind of conflict? Why did you need weapons then?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Milosevic, what was asked for was a legal increase in the police force, because our area, Bosanska Krajina, had been destabilised a lot earlier before the war conflict actually started in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Due to the conflicts in Croatia, all of this was reflected in our area, Bosanska Krajina, and almost for one year people could not travel through the part of Croatia called the Serb Krajina. Some people were even killed when they tried to travel through that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you linked this to what happened in Krajina, let me mention something that did not happen in Krajina, that happened in your region, as a matter of fact. You certainly remember when the following happened: In 1991, in Bosanska Krupa, when a monument disappeared, the monument dedicated to the author Branko Copic, and it was supposed to be placed close to the public security station building and it simply disappeared.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The monument did not disappear, Mr. Izetbegovic [sic]. It cannot be treated that way. This is something that happened actually at the beginning of 1991. The dispute over the monument started because the permit to place the monument there had been issued against the law, illegally. All of this was done by the then-president of the SDS, Miroslav Vjestica, as secretary of the Secretariat for Social Services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Already twice you've addressed me as Mr. Itzetbegovic. It's probably your subconsciousness speaking. You probably have some reason for that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You're trying to say that this was organised by the secretary of the Secretariat for Social Services. Is it true that the monument was stolen from the very centre of town during the night?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course that's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what happened to the monument?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the monument never existed. When the preparations started to build the base for the monument, a procedure was started to annul the permit that had been issued illegally. So then the authorities in charge said that the entire activity should be halted. Just before the first church service was supposed to be held in the Orthodox church in Bosanska Krupa - and I can't remember exactly on which date this was - persons unknown left a bust of Branko Copic right next to the place where the works had started. As far as I can remember, this bust was removed by the authorities in charge in a legal way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this led to inter-ethnic tensions because of which a meeting was held among the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina attended by Alija Izetbegovic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Ejub Ganic, Avdo Hebic [phoen], Halil Delimustafic, Mehmed Mahic, and Suad Alibegic, officials from your municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were certain tensions. I think that that is why the whole thing was prepared as such, to bring yet another thing into the situation that prevailed at the time that would lead to further destabilisation. Actually, the representatives of the SDS and the local representatives of the Orthodox church in Bosanska Krupa visited the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they launched the initiative to have such a meeting held. The meeting was not actually held in the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina because the representatives of the SDS did not wish to participate in the meeting until the then-president of the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Karadzic, withdrew the statements that he made on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. TV Bosnia-Herzegovina in this respect, and what he said was wrong. As far as I know, only a press conference was held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mladen Drljaca, a Serb, attended this meeting and for a while he was secretary of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat yet again there was no official meeting held, only a press conference was held. As for Mladen Drljaca, Mr. Mladen Drljaca, I know him personally, I do not remember that he was present there. I don't remember him coming to Sarajevo, because I was one of the representatives of the SDA from Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended the press conference, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know, then, since this was not held as an official meeting, that Ejub Ganic at this meeting, not knowing that Mladen Drljaca was a Serb, said to Mehmed Mahic that, "All these Serbs should be cleansed." Did Mahic inform you about that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, Mahic Mehmed was not present at this press conference, and he was not on the delegation of the SDA of Bosanska Krupa that was supposed to participate at the planned meeting. As a matter of fact, we concluded in Bosanska Krupa that it would not be right for the official representatives of the authorities from Bosanska Krupa to attend the meeting because that could be interpreted as pressure against these representatives of the authorities in resolving this particular case. So practically only Mr. Kabijevic [phoen] and I were sent to attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you know that Ejub Ganic then said that all these Serbs should be cleansed.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was no meeting, that means that I cannot be aware of what you say just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you don't know, then just say that you don't know and let's move on. On the same day after the meeting was held, the monument was found at the chapel of the municipal cemetery in Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a meeting that was held in Bosanska Krupa itself, this was a day before the church service at the Orthodox church, the bust of Branko Copic was handed over to the gentleman who had actually financed the building of the monument. He actually ordered this bust. He commissioned it. And I assume that this was at the chapel of the cemetery in Bosanska Krupa. And also, there was a written argument -- agreement that he should keep the bust in his garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, page 6, you refer to what happened in the village of Arapusa. You call it an incident.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that on that occasion that there was a bit of shooting and that a young Serb was wounded.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about this indirectly. Mr. Mehmed Mahic, president of the municipal Assembly, was involved in the entire course of these talks, and I can only convey the information I learned from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you certainly know that three young Serbs were wounded, gravely at that, from firearms.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, Mr. Milosevic. As I said, I can only have information that I received from others in this regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say some shooting, but -- that means an exchange of gunfire, but these young men were ambushed. There was no exchange of gunfire. Don't you know that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I received, there was some shooting. It was a skirmish because this happened during the night. Arapusa was a village that was populated by Bosniaks only. These young men, who were driving in a car through the village, came a cross a checkpoint of the reserve police force. As far as I was informed, there was a skirmish, there was an exchange of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this same paragraph on page 6, you say that this was staged by the SDS in order to cause an incident.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I believed then, and I still believe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you believe that the SDS sent young Serbs to a Muslim village and also that the SDS sent members of the Muslim police force to go to that village and to shoot at these young Serbs and to seriously wound or kill these young Serbs, because those men who were in the ambush could not have known whether they killed them or not, so that they could afterwards attack Bosanska Krupa. So is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said and that's not what I'm trying to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say the SDS staged this. So they sent these young men there and they probably sent the Muslim police to shoot at them.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are speculations, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can it be speculation if it says in paragraph 2, page 6, that it was staged by the SDS, this shooting at the young Serb men?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already answered this question. If you need additional explanation, I would kindly ask you to say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Your brother knew then and knows now who exactly shot at these young men, but nothing was ever done. The police was under his command. Nothing was done to arrest the perpetrators and to calm down the inter-ethnic tension that resulted.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Milosevic, this incident took place two days before the attack on Bosanska Krupa. Whether measures had been taken against these reserve policemen, I don't know, because already on the 21st of April -- and I must say that in the meantime, between the 19th and the 21st of April, SDS representatives did not show up for planned meetings and negotiations in Bosanska Krupa, and I had no information from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you say in another paragraph on page 6 that the SDS reacted to this incident by sending their paramilitaries to this village to surround the village. Was it an organised action of the paramilitaries of the SDS or was it just a spontaneous reaction of the local residents?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, a representative of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa went immediately to that village on a visit - I'm speaking about Mehmed Mahic, president of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanska Krupa - and from talking to him, I learned that he toured the village in the presence of Gojko Klickovic, president of the Crisis Staff that had been formed by the SDS. When they were touring the village, they were able to clearly see, in fact, Mr. Mahic clearly saw armed paramilitaries, and he had the impression that they were commanded by Mr. Klickovic. He even told me that when touring this area, one of the members of the paramilitary units, whether deliberately or not, fired a volley of automatic fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during this siege, as you call it, nobody was wounded or killed. The only demand was made to surrender to the police, and I repeat, the police, not local residents, the perpetrators of the crime against young Serb men.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were responsible for this incident - and I'm not going to call it a crime - were available to the police from the very beginning, but I cannot agree with you when you say that in this operation of the paramilitaries, the Serb paramilitaries, nobody was killed. Arapusa remained under seige for the next two days and even after the attack on Bosanska Krupa. All civilians were subsequently driven away from their homes, and some people, at least two of whom I can name, went missing. They were taken to concentration camps and were never seen again. These two people are Ibrahim Ibrahimovic, and Sulejman Ibrahimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know about these camps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have two minutes left now, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would appreciate short answers, Mr. Velic. I have just a few more questions. It will take two or three minutes. On the 21st of April, 1992, a meeting was held in Bosanska Krupa Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to discuss this incident, and it was attended by General Spiro Ninkovic from the 10th Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. It was his liaison officer who arrived. I don't know his name. He was a captain by rank. And Mr. Spiro Ninkovic turned up just in time for the beginning of the meeting. He did not want to attend the meeting, he only wanted to talk to the president of the Assembly, Mr. Mehmed Mahic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it true that he came to Bosanska Krupa to talk to the local authorities who were then located in Jasenica village in order to convey the position, the message of Blagoje Adzic, chief of the General Staff, that every effort must be made to defuse the tensions that occurred after the incident of the killing of Serb men?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that, but I can say that Mr. Ninkovic left the building accompanied by Mr. Mahic, and he went on to visit the village of Vranjska and Jasenica. However, a couple of minutes after Mr. Mahic returned to the building, the shelling of Bosanska Krupa began precisely from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that two kilometres away from the entrance to Bosanska Krupa the vehicle containing Ninkovic and his entourage came under fire from automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that that is true. Muslim positions did not exist then. There was only a police checkpoint at the exit from the town. He passed through that checkpoint accompanied by Mr. Mahic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely during -- due to the fact that fire was opened against him, he wanted to be escorted.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was then, as you say, that the attack on Krupa occurred, and shooting continued throughout that night.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the shooting lasted for about an hour, and then there was a lull. There were no more activities, no more operations during the night, and the shelling resumed at 6:00 a.m. the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it who opened fire at Bosanska Krupa then?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot name any names and I cannot tell you anything specific; I can only tell you what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't see anything. But is it clear to you that it wasn't the JNA that was firing?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that it was the armed formations of the SDS firing from guns of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This must be your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not the JNA that attacked the town. On the contrary. At the meeting of the 25th of April attended by Fikret Abdic, Miroslav Vjestica, and others, General Spiro Ninkovic suggested that neutral areas, neutral zones, be established to prevent this from re-occurring.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended another meeting in Bosanski Petrovac which was another attempt to discuss the case of Bosanska Krupa. This meeting in Bosanski Petrovac was indeed attended by General Spiro Ninkovic as well as Fikret Abdic. The talks that took place at that meeting were too vague, unspecific. General Spiro Ninkovic did speak about some kind of role for the army, but he made no specific proposals. We thought that the case could be resolved within the institutions of the system without any participation or involvement of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's your last question. Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that there is one thing that remains unclarified with regard to the statement of this witness. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you would be so kind, Witness, look at the last paragraph on page 8 where you spoke first about the meeting between the SDS and the SDA, which turned out to be the last meeting. You did not mention any negotiations with the JNA, and then you say: "The front lines around Bosanska Krupa narrowed. The town was divided into two parts. The Una River became a front line. In that period, there were no serious attempts on the part of Serbian forces to capture the left bank. They seemed to be content with the territory they held at the moment." And then you mention further on that you discussed possible ways of defending yourself. My question is: This defence line, this front line, existed between your forces and the forces of the SDS, that is your paramilitaries and their paramilitaries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. My microphone wasn't working. "Front line" is not a term I would use, and it certainly does not correspond to the situation on the ground in Bosanska Krupa at the time. You say that the participation of the JNA in that meeting is not mentioned, but what is mentioned is the presence of General Ninkovic and his specific proposals. As for front lines, they did not exist in the true military sense of the word. There were only police forces in Bosanska Krupa who were disorganised over a period of three or four days that followed, and there was a certain number of volunteers, if I can call them that, who self-organised in order to defend the town. I can accept that the remaining part of your quotation is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do speak about front lines and the division of the town in two parts. Then you say in the next paragraph they managed -- in fact: "We managed to hold these lines until November 1992. Serbs moved to the left bank and captured some parts of the town." Could you explain this?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. After a few days in which chaos reigned in that part of the town on the left bank of the Una River, the population of Bosanska Krupa withdrew to the left bank of the Una River, and that situation continued for the few months that followed. And then the events that I mentioned already occurred. I wasn't in town any more, but the information that I quoted here is information I received from others who did live there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because at that time, you were in the War Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was located in Zagreb at the time. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a completely wrong interpretation of what I said. I was in Zagreb according to the decision of the War Presidency of Bosanska Krupa. I was sent to Zagreb on a certain mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not true if it says here: "I left Bosanska Krupa in November 1992. I was sent to Zagreb to work in the War Presidency."

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. The War Presidency was located in Bosanska Krupa. It should say, "... according to the decision of the War Presidency." I don't know how this error found its way into my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. With permission, I'd just like to ask a few questions in re-examination Re-examined by Mr. Agha:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, in your evidence you mention that you were shown a study on the administration division of Bosanska Krupa as being the first steps in creating a Balkan state. Do you remember that study? Now, how many other municipalities were shown similar studies like that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention that study which in everyday talk we referred to as the feasibility study on the division of the Bosanska Krupa municipality. The official title was probably different. It was not a step towards forming a phantom state. It said in the first paragraph of the study it was -- it said it was the first step to the establishment of the first unified Serbian state in the Balkans. I later learned that a similar study was done for the municipality of Bihac, and in subsequent informal contacts, I found out that in municipalities with mixed population - mixed consisting of Serbs, Croats, Bosniaks, and others - the SDS suggested and offered similar studies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I think this is quite an important point which the Trial Chamber would like to know about, and being a lawyer and one of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. leading SDA people, perhaps you can help. You refer in your evidence that there was a decision of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency that no one should join the JNA. At that time, which ethnic groups made up the Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That happened during the events in Croatia in 1991. At that time, there were seven members of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, including representatives of the three constituent peoples, because there were three constituent peoples at that time, Serbs, Muslims, and Croats, plus one representative of the group called Yugoslavs; that is, there were seven members in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that decision, who was it legally binding on in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That decision of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina was, of course, binding on all authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina that were subordinated to the Presidency including, of course, Secretariats for National Defence in various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would include the Muslim, Serbian, and Croatian population; everybody?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, because the authorities, the bodies of administration, the bodies of government in Bosnia and Herzegovina, were unified and single, and they were elected after multi-party elections in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I have one final question for you, is that you mention that the mosque and the Catholic church on the bank of the Una, which the Serbian forces were occupying at Bosanska Krupa, were destroyed. What was the fate of the Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the buildings that you mentioned are at most 100 metres away from each other in Bosanska Krupa. The mosque was set on fire as soon as Serb forces entered Bosanska Krupa. The Catholic church was destroyed under circumstances that I'm not familiar with because I only saw that when I returned to Bosanska Krupa after the war, and the Serbian Orthodox Church remained intact, in the condition in which it is still today.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: That completes my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Velic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go. If you would just wait one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to avail myself of this idle time to ask you a question. I received this schedule. It says 9th December to be decided. Are we sitting on the 9th or not? I am not clear on that, because I need to know for purposes of my own planning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is undecided. It depends on the health of Judge Robinson. You should keep it clear for sitting. If he is fit enough, we will sit. Otherwise, we won't. But I'm afraid we can't make a firm decision on that because, as I say, it depends on his health.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness -- I'm not sure whether we're in private or open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We can be in open session, there is no problem. The next witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next witness is Mr. Deronjic. We haven't made a formal written application to have his statement admitted under 89(F). The Chamber will possibly recall that we first, I think, provided draft copies of his statement before the order to make written applications was made, and we didn't get a final signed version until yesterday. The position on disclosure of his material is as follows: Leave was granted to call him on the 16th of October, and in anticipation of that, transcripts of his interviews have been disclosed on the 10th of October. The first draft of his statement in English was provided on the 13th of November, and much of that cross-referred to his interviews. Another draft in English and B/C/S was provided on the 24th of November. The witness signed the statement with minor amendments yesterday, and that was provided in English and B/C/S yesterday, the Chamber having had the earlier draft version and having had, I hope now by the form of a memorandum, a notice of the very limited changes to some six paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will admit the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very grateful. The statement deals with a large number of matters. The witness has given evidence twice recently publicly, once as recently as last week. In the interests of saving time, and unless the Court orders otherwise, I would not propose necessarily to take him through any of his evidence in chief, although I might ask him simply one or two general questions and get him to produce one exhibit additional to those that have already been produced by other witnesses. I don't know if that approach is acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: My name is Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, it's a matter of public record that you have entered pleas of guilty at this Tribunal in respect of an indictment and are awaiting sentence in respect of matters to which you've pleaded guilty; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already given evidence before component parts of this Tribunal on two previous occasions and have cooperated with the Tribunal in the preparation of an extensive witness statement, now in some 232 paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You reviewed that statement in your own language in the course of the last couple of days and signed a version of it and signed every page of that version yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is also correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that statement and its contents true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: This statement is completely accurate, and I agreed to sign it as a completely accurate statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It should be given the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 600, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your statement, you identify really four exhibits, three of them exhibits that have been produced before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for purposes of ease of reference, can I deal with those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At paragraph 45, Mr. Deronjic, you dealt with the question of Variant A and B municipalities, as described, and with instructions that had been disseminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that's Exhibit 434, tab 3. I don't desire to go through it, I'm just doing this for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At paragraph 68 of your statement, you dealt with the question of the strategic goals of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the document that sets out those strategic goals is Exhibit 451, tab 12. At paragraph 224, just to deal with exhibits already produced, you dealt with the document signed eventually by Mr. Franken after he'd amended it. And we've heard from Mr. Franken recently, and that document is Exhibit 591, tab 9. Have you reviewed those three exhibits and do you confirm that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. those are the documents to which you were referring?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I looked at all three documents, and these are the documents that you referred to just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not - it's my mistake. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should tell you, Mr. Deronjic, that the Trial Chamber has agreed to accept your statement in full as your evidence-in-chief so that I'm going to be asking a very limited number of questions and we'll be moving rapidly to cross-examination. But before I do that, there is the one additional exhibit that I want to produce through you, and you're entitled to look at your witness statement at any point, subject to the decision of the Trial Chamber, if you wish to. And at paragraph 206, dealing with both the evacuations and executions that occurred on the 13th of July, 1995, you speak of a phone call that you made to Karadzic. And if you please look at the exhibit that is presently before you, which is a transcript of an intercept of a telephone conversation between you and Karadzic, have you reviewed the transcript of that intercept?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have reviewed that transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you in a position to help us whether that appears to be an accurate transcript of a conversation you had with Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is an accurate transcript of the conversation that I had with Mr. Karadzic on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the usher would be good enough just to place the first page of the English version of this on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, we find in this transcript of the intercept reference to -- at the bottom of the page if we see it, part of the conversation goes -- "Can you hear me, President?" Somebody saying, "The president can't hear, Deronjic, this is the intermediary." And you saying: "I have 2000 here now by ..." and then your voice was drowned out, and then X says: "Deronjic, the president says: 'All the goods must be placed in the warehouse before 12 tomorrow.'" "Right." X says: "Deronjic, not in the warehouses but somewhere else." You say, "Understood." And if we can then go to the next page. It says: "I'm waiting for a call to President Karadzic. Is he there?" "Yes." "Hello. Just a minute, the duty officer will answer you now, Mr. President." "Hello, I have Deronjic on the line," and then you speak to him. "Hello. I can hear you." "Deronjic, the president is asking how many thousands." You say: "Two for the time being but there will be more during the night." Now, what was being referred to as goods and by the number of 2.000, if you can help us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: The goods that are mentioned, or the 2.000 mentioned in terms of figures, pertained to the imprisoned Muslims who were brought to Bratunac during the night of the 13th, and they were put up at various localities including the elementary school, the hangar, the stadium, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May this transcript of an intercept be admitted, either fully admitted or admitted for identification purposes, but the acknowledgement by the witness of its accuracy may take it into the position of being an exhibit that can be fully produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: At this stage we're going to mark it for identification because we're going to have evidence about these intercepts in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, give it the next number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 601, Your Honour, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I'm mistaken, but I have not received either on tape or on CD this intercepted conversation, so I would kindly ask to have this provided for me if it exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll deal with that over the break and check whether it's one of those that has been provided; and if not, I'll find out why not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, your statement, which is now an exhibit in the case, covers a range of matters from the arming of the Serbs to your particular position as commissioner at Srebrenica and so on. Can you help us, please, by giving, just in a few sentences because you're an educated man, a teacher, of all these events, can you, just in a few sentences, survey the relevant history and explain how it was that people such as you came to be involved in these events. And without leading you but simply reminding you how you've described it in the past, I think you've used the word "spiral" or spiral of events. If you could do it in a few minutes, perhaps up to five, I think that would be very helpful for us.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will try to answer this question. You have noticed that my statement contains events ranging over a period of almost five years, that is to say from 1990 until 1995. In that statement, I tried to focus on the events that I participated in directly, namely the events in Bratunac with reference to what was happening in the neighbouring municipalities to the extent to which I followed these events and was aware of them. Also, I gave a broader survey of political activities, from the lowest level, where I acted for the most part, all the way up to the top level where I took part in 1993 as a member of the Main Board of the SDS. Of course that is a question that preoccupied me, like many other people: What really happened in that area, including the entire area of Bosnia-Herzegovina? As I made this statement, I actually wanted to testify about the following: First and foremost, the events that took place are well known, and the political concepts of the Serbs, Muslims, and Croats are well known in the early 1990s in the absolute crisis that the former Yugoslavia was engulfed in. What led me and many people to take part in these events were the plans that were fully public in their first stage. Now I'm talking about the plans of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They pertained to the need that all Serbs should remain together in one state. At first this was an endeavour to preserve a single Yugoslavia, and after that, these plans were somewhat changed as events developed. This is something that is well known in this Tribunal as well. What did I try to show now throughout my statement: First and foremost, that these public plans that I was involved in too from 1991 onwards, actually related to the establishment of an entity of the Bosnian Serbs in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They are known as the plan to create Republika Srpska. This was a public plan. There were many manifestations related to this plan. This was recorded in the media, in speeches made by top people, including some of the activities I had at local level primarily in the area where I lived and worked. These plans involved certain stages in their implementation. At first it was communities of municipalities that were established and later on they grew into those well-known Serb autonomous regions. There were five of them in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They were formed in the period of 1991, and in the autumn they were verified at an Assembly, at a Serb Assembly, as regions that were roughly supposed to grow into this Serb entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Towards the end of 1991, I took part in these events to an extent to which this surprised most people who were -- there were some measures involved that surprised most people who were involved in political activities in those days. These were the first secret measures that were taken and that were supposed to contribute to the attainment of this objective, namely the establishment of a Serb entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This Tribunal knows about them as Variants A and B. This is what all the party authorities of the SDS in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina received this at the time, with the obligation of carrying this out in the field. These political orders were strictly confidential, highly Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. confidential, and it was the first time ever during my involvement in politics that I then received this kind of paper that was strictly confidential and marked as such. Namely, it was the executive and legislative branches that were supposed to be divided in municipalities. This primarily had to do with minority municipalities. When I say "minority municipalities," that is where Serbs were minority, and there were such municipalities. Bratunac, Zvornik, Srebrenica, Visegrad, not to mention any others. This was within the Serb autonomous regions that I spoke of earlier on. After that, and I have to say this for the sake of the truth, people in various areas interpreted this in different ways and implemented it in different ways. There was even resistance to it, and people tried to adjust to the local situation. And I described the way in which I carried out these instructions. This was a rather special way. I carried out this in Bratunac in the joint Assembly in agreement with representatives of the Muslims in the joint Assembly of the municipality of Bratunac. I just insisted on the singling out of one particular group, and that was the police in Bratunac. So I know that there were special situations in Zvornik too. I knew the leadership very well there too and also in some other municipalities. In this situation, the beginning of April 1992, certain military formations known as the volunteers of Arkan's guard arrived in these areas as well as Seselj's volunteers, and so on and so forth, not to mention all of them. They arrived in the Drina region and some other areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they caused conflicts. For many people, this came as a surprise. I'm not going to talk about myself now but I know some of the things that happened in Zvornik, some of the things that happened in Bijeljina. I know that some Serb leaders were arrested, beaten, kept in prison, tortured, et cetera. So this was a radical stage in the inter-ethnic relations in that area, including the municipality of Bratunac. When these people arrived, they were supposed to constitute a secret part of these plans. So a certain number of people, I cannot say how many, within the SDS leadership itself was not aware of such plans. What happened later, in my opinion, is only a matter of cause and consequence in the area, cause and effect. Quite briefly, when these volunteers in these units from Serbia came to the area, they started killing people, looting. They brought panic to these municipalities, and the inter-ethnic relations that were already threatened led to growing fear and predominantly Muslims started fleeing from the area. Now I'm going to focus on Bratunac because I am most familiar with the situation there. It was to be expected that the Muslims would not simply sit and watch all these things that were happening. Soon after these people came to this region, Naser in Srebrenica, in the village of Potocari, on the 20th of April ambushed these units and killed these men. I don't know exactly how this incident occurred but I know that basically most of the men were killed in this ambush, or practically all of them were killed in this ambush, as far as I know. After that, Goran Zekic was killed, who was one of the leading Serbs in the area, in Srebrenica, on the 8th of May. And then on the 9th of the May we already took some steps, and I explain these in detail in my guilty plea or, rather, in the sentencing brief. All of this led to this cause and effect that I already said, and that is how things evolved. Already in 1992, after everything we did in Bratunac, then the Muslims from Srebrenica took action. They attacked the area of Bratunac. There was a lot of fighting there. Great territories were taken, there were many casualties, military and civilian. In 1993 a counter-offensive of the Serbs started in the area of Srebrenica, and then the well-known Morillon affair, and Srebrenica was proclaimed a safe haven of the UN, safe area, on the 13th of April, 1994. In 1994, both sides made efforts to take the entire area. Muslim area -- Muslim forces from Srebrenica made incursions in the Serbia area. Also I managed to see here some orders of lower level and higher level commands, orders issued to Serb forces around Srebrenica. All of this testified to the fact that these people in the safe area were -- their life was supposed to be made impossible by all means. The logical effect -- I say unfortunately this is the logical effect, and I'm not saying it's a normal thing, that was the offensive of the Serb forces in 1995, the attack on Srebrenica and the denouement that occurred. That is a fact that is well known. Several thousand imprisoned Muslims in the area were killed. I wish to show that what happened in Bratunac in the Drina region and in the municipalities that I knew developed according to a domino effect principle. People came from Serbia to that area that had already been hampered by these different political concepts, and inter-ethnic relations were already quite bad, and all of this led to what happened afterwards. And in my opinion, Srebrenica 1995 is a logical finale, the only thing that could be the result of these events. I'm sorry if I took up a lot of time, but this is a very complex issue, and I wanted to cover all these developments in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing simply with that last --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing simply with your last observation about Srebrenica 1995 being a logical finale, the only thing that could result, is that something that you've simply judged looking back or was it something that was in your mind as an observer at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course I was a participant in most of these events, and I explained this in my statement in a very precise manner. Of course I thought about everything that was going on during the war as well. But I drew a great many conclusions after all these events when I had the opportunity of having contacts with the Office of the Prosecutor that went on from 1997 onwards. I saw a series of documents which explained the situation that I was in from various other aspects. Most of these documents, orders, et cetera, were things I was not aware of at the time when I was engaged in my work that had to do with the war conflict itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that that answers the question, but you say -- whether you thought about these things at the time and thought that something like this was going to happen or not, but if you don't want to answer further, I won't press you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: I have said that I realised many things during the war itself but that I finally came to my own conclusions after the war operations in the area ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. I'm slightly undecided in my own mind whether the Court, having allowed the whole statement to go in, it would be appropriate for me to go through any of the paragraphs. At most I have about four that I might ask the witness to deal with, but can I deal with that after the break, if it's appropriate. Otherwise, we will just let the statement stand and move straight to cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn now for the break. Mr. Deronjic, during your evidence, don't speak to anybody about it, please, until it's over, and that does include any members of the Prosecution. We will adjourn now for 20 minutes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: With Your Honours' leave, I'll identify about six points of evidence in the witness's statement to give additional context for those viewing who haven't read the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, if you would be good enough just to look at the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. appropriate paragraph numbers as I come to them, starting at paragraph 8 where you're dealing with the arming of the Serbs. You speak of what Karadzic told you about a conversation he had with the accused Milosevic about the arming of the Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you put it, what had Karadzic achieved in the discussions with Milosevic about the arming of the Serbs? What had he achieved?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: At that meeting in the village of Milici attended by Dukic, Mr. Zekic, and myself, Mr. Rajko Dukic uttered the following sentence: He said that Mr. Karadzic personally convinced Mr. Milosevic that Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina should be armed. I later had the occasion, and I don't remember the exact date or the form of the meeting with Karadzic, to hear that said from his own mouth, namely that he had persuaded Mr. Milosevic that Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina should be armed. There was some degree of disagreement about the involvement of the army in the possible resolution of the crisis, and I think that is why Mr. Karadzic wanted Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina to be armed. That is what I meant when I said what I said in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Paragraph 63. You made an observation about the pattern of events and the takeover of municipalities where volunteers came first, killings, liquidations, and intimidation followed, and the JNA arrived thereafter but in a short period of time; and your inference from the pattern of events occurring in more than one place was what?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I called it a scheme of developments in Eastern Bosnia, and I am referring to Eastern Bosnia because that's the area I'm most familiar with. There was a certain precise chronology, sequence of developments, of course with certain nuances depending on the peculiarities of a particular community's. I meant, first of all, that these volunteers such as the Arkan's -- the Arkan guards and others would come to the territory before the outbreak of a conflict where inter-ethnic relations had already been disrupted, and we know that by referring to materials known as Variant A and B. The arrival of volunteers would create a certain climate in these areas primarily due to the killings of innocent people, widespread looting, robbing of private property, mainly from people of Muslim faith, resulting in the intimidation of the Muslim community and their fleeing from the area. Those were the complex events that took place in those regions. With the arrival of the army - and we are talking about the JNA since this took place before the 15th of May - created an impression, a false impression maybe, that the JNA would make efforts to prevent these developments. But then from a series of facts, we could see that the Yugoslav People's Army sided with the Serbs, and its activities in those areas contributed to the deepening of inter-ethnic tensions, the fleeing of Muslims from these areas, and as far as I know, in Bratunac municipality and in neighbouring municipalities the JNA took part even in the offensive actions undertaken by Serbs in that territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next paragraph is 136, but it's within a passage that begins, to give you the context, Mr. Deronjic, it begins at paragraph 131 with the Red Berets in Bratunac, and you speak of a meeting possibly in June, possibly July. And then at paragraph 134 you explain that Mr. Simatovic, known as Frenki, was there. And at paragraph 136, and it is only this that I want your evidence on live, because you understand your entire statement is in: Did Frenki Simatovic tell you at what level the task he had to accomplish had been agreed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Frenki, at that time meeting whose exact date I don't know, said that it had been agreed at the highest level, meaning probably the highest political level of the state of Serbia and of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll move on, please, to paragraph 163, by which stage in your statement we are into 1995, and indeed the spring of 1995. You deal with Karadzic touring the regions and scheduling meetings, at one of which he spoke to you and said of Srebrenica what was to come. Can you tell us, just in a sentence or so, what it was that Karadzic told you about what was to come for Srebrenica as of that date, spring of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first I ever learnt of that, namely that in Bratunac, a neighbouring municipality to Srebrenica, certain military activities would take place. He didn't say exactly which activities, but he said certain military activities would be undertaken there, and I should, if I deem it necessary, undertake the necessary preparations in my area. Those were his words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what if anything did he say specifically about what was going to happen in Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: At that moment, he did not say anything. He said some military activities would be carried out around Srebrenica, that I should not talk about it to anyone, that he was not going to divulge any details, but if I thought it necessary, I should carry out some preparations such as making sure that we had enough oil supplies and supplies of other commodities, the usual routine activities related to the army, without explaining precisely what was about to happen in Srebrenica in the military sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About two or three more references at most. The next one, please, at paragraph 175 when you are dealing with a meeting of the 9th of July in Pale. You saw Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- but you also saw another man, and at paragraph 175, you deal with how he was introduced to you and who he was.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC
utterances.text: The person in question was Mr. Jovica Stanisic. I said that I had been introduced to him in such a way that I understood that they had been discussing Srebrenica at their preceding meeting, and I attended the following meeting on the 8th or the 9th when I received confirmation, new confirmation that the topic of their talks was Srebrenica. And he introduced me as one of their people from the area, from the ground, meaning Srebrenica. And the way he phrased it confirms that they had been discussing Srebrenica at the meeting that they had just had.
